bihar_raw_news.title: "Did not receive special package for floods;": Tejashwi Yadav targets PM Modi ahead his Bihar visit
bihar_raw_news.content: "Did not receive special package for floods;": Tejashwi Yadav targets PM Modi ahead his Bihar visit ANI | Updated: Nov 06, 2026 01:37 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], November 6 (ANI): Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Thursday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of his upcoming visit to the state, alleging that Bihar had not received adequate support from the Centre and that the state government had failed to address issues such as crime, education and healthcare. Yadav said the people of Bihar had given the Prime Minister a massive mandate but continued to be treated like "stepchildren" whenever the state needed assistance. "The Prime Minister is coming to Bihar, yet he has failed to fulfil any of the duties expected of a Prime Minister. The people of Bihar gave him a massive mandate, but whenever Bihar is in need, we are treated like stepchildren. We did not receive a special package for the floods; the Bihar government's coffers are empty. Of the 'double-engine' government, one engine is fuelled by corruption, while the other is driven by crime; an atmosphere of anarchy has taken hold in Bihar. Now that he is visiting, he will surely resort to empty rhetoric," he said. Questioning the development record of the state government, the RJD leader said Bihar continued to rank at the bottom across sectors, including education and healthcare, citing NITI Aayog reports. "They (the ruling side) always repeat the same rehearsed lines. How long has Narendra Modi held the office of Prime Minister? His government has been in power here consistently. NITI Aayog reports indicate that we rank at the very bottom across all sectors—from education to healthcare. The situation remains exactly the same today; there has been no improvement whatsoever," Yadav said. He also criticised Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary over the law-and-order situation in the state, questioning the government's response to incidents of crime across districts. "Is there any district here where crime does not occur? Yet, we have a Chief Minister who seems to think that the terms 'apradh' and crime are different things. One is an English word, and the other is a Hindi word, but the meaning is exactly the same. He is making Bihar a laughing stock. What can one expect from such a Chief Minister? What will become of Bihar?" he said. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Industrial Policy Gets Push With Monthly Business Meets - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Industrial Policy Gets Push as CM Orders Monthly Business Meets Breaking News Bihar Industrial Policy Gets Push as CM Orders Monthly Business Meets By Harpreet Singh November 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed the state industries minister and district authorities to hold regular meetings with entrepreneurs, signalling a faster grievance-redressal approach for businesses operating across the state. The instruction was issued at the 82nd annual function of the Bihar Industries Association (BIA), which the chief minister inaugurated. Choudhary asked Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh to conduct monthly meetings with entrepreneurs and ensure that their suggestions are considered while framing industrial policies. He also urged district magistrates and superintendents of police to organise similar interactions with entrepreneurs in their respective districts. The directions place district-level administration at the centre of Bihar’s effort to address industrial concerns. The proposed meetings are intended to provide a formal channel for businesses to raise issues and seek quicker resolution from officials responsible for local administration, land and law-and-order matters. Speaking at the event, Choudhary said nearly 1,000 industrial units had moved to the implementation stage during the past year. The statement did not provide a district-wise breakdown of these units or specify the investment value and employment potential associated with them. The chief minister also said several long-pending issues connected with Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority land had been resolved. He referred to the introduction of a new land allotment and management policy, but the details of the policy, including its operational provisions and implementation timeline, were not provided in the supplied report. Industrial land administration has been a recurring concern for businesses because the availability, allotment and management of land influence whether proposed projects can move from announcement to implementation. By linking entrepreneur meetings with district officials and the industries department, the government is seeking to create more direct administrative engagement around such concerns. The event also brought a specific policy request from industry representatives. In response to the demand for a dedicated pharmaceutical policy, Choudhary asked entrepreneurs to prepare a draft proposal and submit it to the government for consideration. The next step, therefore, rests with the industry to frame and send the proposal before the state examines it. Singh attended the BIA function as chief guest. The association also presented its 2025-26 memorial awards to Patel Agri Industries, Banke Bihari Foods, Badshah Industries and former BIA president Arun Agrawal for their contributions to the sector. The government’s immediate implementation milestones are the proposed monthly meetings led by the industries minister, similar district-level interactions involving district magistrates and police superintendents, and the submission of the pharmaceutical policy draft by entrepreneurs. bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During Modi’s Vaishali Visit Breaking News Patna-Purnia Expressway May Get Launch Nod During Modi’s Vaishali Visit By Harpreet Singh November 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to address a public meeting in Vaishali on November 21, where he may formally inaugurate construction work on the Patna-Purnia Expressway, Bihar’s proposed first national expressway. The six-lane greenfield project is planned to connect Vaishali with Purnia through five districts and could become a major addition to the state’s east-west road network. The public meeting will be held at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area in Vaishali district, BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi said after a meeting of National Democratic Alliance constituents at the chief minister’s residence. The visit is planned around the completion of one year of the Bihar NDA government’s present term on November 20. Saraogi said the Prime Minister’s visit was expected to bring new projects for Bihar, but the available announcement does not establish that all the proposed projects will receive final approval or inauguration during the event. The Patna-Purnia Expressway is among the projects expected to feature prominently in the programme. The proposed expressway will begin at Mirnagar on NH-22 in Vaishali district and pass through Samastipur, Darbhanga, Saharsa and Madhepura before reaching Chand Bhatti on NH-27 in Purnia. The planned six-lane, greenfield alignment is intended to create a faster road connection across north and eastern Bihar, linking districts that currently depend heavily on existing highways and local road networks. The project’s significance lies in the scale of the proposed corridor and its potential role in connecting urban centres, district headquarters and rural production areas. However, the source report does not provide the expressway’s approved cost, total length, land-acquisition status, construction schedule or traffic projections. Those details will be important in determining how quickly the corridor can move from a political announcement to implementation. Modi may also inaugurate or lay the foundation stones for other projects in Bhagalpur and Banka districts. These could include a proposed central university near Vikramshila and the proposed Ajgaibinath Greenfield Airport near Sultanganj in Bhagalpur district. The report does not specify their project costs, land requirements or expected completion timelines. The Prime Minister’s visit is also being organised against the backdrop of discussions within the NDA following the Janata Dal (United)’s defeat in three of four seats in the October 23 legislative council elections. Saraogi said the alliance meeting focused on preparations for the visit, while JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha said the alliance remained intact and that the relationship between the BJP and JD(U) had endured for two decades. Kushwaha added that the party had collected feedback from district units about the election results. Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) state president Surendra Vivek also said there was no resentment within the alliance. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Fast-Tracks VB-G RAM G With 3 Lakh Rural Projects - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Fast-Tracks VB-G RAM G With 3 Lakh Rural Projects Breaking News Bihar Fast-Tracks VB-G RAM G With 3 Lakh Rural Projects By Harpreet Singh November 6, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed officials to accelerate the rollout of the Viksit Bharat-Rozgar evam Aajeevika Guarantee Mission-Rural, or VB-G RAM G, with the state targeting 3 lakh projects worth Rs 22,000 crore for rural employment and village development. Chairing a review meeting on Thursday, Choudhary stressed that rural households should receive 125 days of guaranteed employment annually under the mission. He also instructed officials to ensure that wages are paid within 15 days, making timely disbursal a central implementation priority. The number of projects planned under the mission is to be increased from 1.5 lakh to 3 lakh. According to the state government, the programme is intended to support rural employment, strengthen livelihoods and advance infrastructure development across villages. The chief minister identified water security, rural infrastructure, livelihood enhancement and disaster management as the four key intervention areas. The planned works include Anganwadi centres, additional classrooms in schools, healthcare facilities, rural markets and playgrounds. The programme will also cover the renovation of canals, reservoirs and other water bodies. These projects place water management and basic public infrastructure within the same employment and village development framework, according to the details presented at the meeting. The state has set a specific construction and furnishing allocation for Anganwadi centres. Each centre will receive Rs 12 lakh for construction, along with an additional Rs 2 lakh for furnishings, educational materials and furniture. Rural Development Department Additional Chief Secretary H R Srinivas presented the mission’s features, action plan and implementation strategy during the review. The meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Building Construction Department Minister Leshi Singh and senior departmental officials. The scale-up places responsibility on district and local implementation systems to identify works, execute projects and process wage payments within the stated timeline. The government’s emphasis on water bodies, schools, healthcare facilities and village markets also links employment generation with the delivery of community assets. The state government said effective implementation of VB-G RAM G would provide fresh momentum to the comprehensive development of villages. The next stage is the incorporation and execution of the expanded project list under the mission, alongside monitoring of wage payments and the identified priority works. national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said India expects to exceed its 220 billion dollar investment target for adding 190 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030. Addressing the media at the conclusion of the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit 2026, the Union Minister said that investments totalling 7 lakh crore rupees, including domestic funds and foreign direct investment, have flowed into the renewable energy sector over the past two years. Mr Joshi said the momentum would continue and India would meet the 500 GW target on schedule. He added that strategies are also being prepared to add another 300 GW as directed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said that at present, the country’s installed power capacity from non-fossil fuels stands at 310 GW, and the Union government has fixed a target of reaching 500 GW by 2030. Meanwhile, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Secretary, Santosh Kumar Sarangi said the government is preparing new guidelines for recycling solar module waste. The Summit was inaugurated by Prime Minister on 2nd November 2026. In his address, the Prime Minister highlighted the strategic importance of India’s sustained investments in renewable energy in strengthening the country’s resilience to global disruptions, arising from COVID-19 pandemic and the West Asia crisis. He observed that India’s investment in the renewable energy sector has largely shielded the country from these disruptions.

national_raw_news.title: From snow leopards to coral reefs: India’s biosphere reserves connect conservation with livelihoods
national_raw_news.content: In the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, an invasive shrub is finding a second life as elephant sculptures, furniture and handicrafts. Indigenous artisans use uprooted Lantana vines to create objects that support livelihoods while drawing attention to the damage the plant causes to forests. In 2021, 125 life-sized Lantana elephants were displayed in London, carrying a message of coexistence with wildlife. Similar sculptures have appeared at Bengaluru Airport, across Bengaluru and at Rashtrapati Bhavan. The initiative illustrates the idea at the heart of biosphere reserves: protecting nature while creating opportunities for the people who depend on it. As the International Day for Biosphere Reserves is observed on November 3, India’s network of 18 notified reserves demonstrates how conservation, scientific research and sustainable livelihoods can work together. Thirteen of these reserves belong to UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves, the highest number in South Asia. The landscapes range from the forests of the Western Ghats and the mangroves of the Sundarbans to the coral reefs of the Gulf of Mannar and the high-altitude Cold Desert of Himachal Pradesh. Conservation beyond protected boundaries India is one of the world’s 17 mega-biodiverse countries. Despite occupying only 2.4 per cent of Earth’s land area, it accounts for approximately 7–8 per cent of recorded species worldwide. Protecting this diversity requires attention to habitats, species and genetic variation, alongside the needs of communities that rely on natural resources. Biosphere reserves provide a framework for bringing these objectives together. While national parks and wildlife sanctuaries primarily protect wildlife and habitats under India’s wildlife protection laws, biosphere reserves take a broader approach, connecting protected ecosystems with surrounding settlements and economic activities. UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere Programme, launched in 1971, promotes scientific approaches to improving relationships between people and their environment. Biosphere reserves serve as living laboratories where sustainable development practices can be tested and demonstrated. Their work combines three functions: conserving biodiversity and landscapes, supporting environmentally responsible economic development, and advancing research, monitoring, education and training. Three zones, connected purposes A biosphere reserve’s structure reflects this balance. Its core area provides the highest level of protection, conserving habitats, species and genetic resources. Human activity is strictly limited, with compatible research and monitoring supporting conservation. The surrounding or adjoining buffer zone accommodates activities such as environmental education, scientific research and regulated ecotourism. These help build ecological understanding while reducing pressure on the core. The transition area supports settlements and livelihoods, including responsible agriculture, sustainable forestry and locally appropriate tourism. Globally, core areas account for an average of 18 per cent of biosphere reserves, buffer zones for 30 per cent and transition areas for 52 per cent. The distribution underlines the importance of inhabited, working landscapes within the conservation model. A network spanning India’s ecological diversity Nilgiri, designated in 1986, was India’s first biosphere reserve. It entered UNESCO’s World Network in 2000. Spread across 5,520 square kilometres in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, the reserve includes tropical evergreen forests, montane shola forests and grasslands. Its wildlife includes the endangered lion-tailed macaque and Nilgiri tahr, as well as elephants, tigers, gaur, sambar and chital. The landscape supports more than 100 mammal species and 550 bird species. At a different ecological extreme, Himachal Pradesh’s Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve covers 7,770 square kilometres at elevations between 3,300 and 6,600 metres. Included in UNESCO’s network in 2025, it supports snow leopards, Himalayan ibex and blue sheep, alongside 732 vascular plant species, including 30 endemics. Around 12,000 people live in this demanding environment. Their livelihoods draw on pastoralism, yak and goat herding, barley and pea cultivation, and Tibetan herbal medicine. Off Tamil Nadu’s southeastern coast, the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve brings together coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangroves across approximately 10,500 square kilometres. These linked ecosystems support 4,223 plant and animal species. The reserve sustains around 25 lakh people across a region that includes approximately 47 coastal villages. The other Indian reserves recognised by UNESCO are Nanda Devi, Nokrek, Sundarbans, Great Nicobar, Similipal, Pachmarhi, Khangchendzonga, Agasthyamalai, Achanakmar-Amarkantak and Panna. Manas, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dehang-Dibang, Great Rann of Kutch and Seshachalam complete India’s nationally notified network.
